original.target_description: Problem 11: Risky Plan N choice in specific $250,000 goal versus do-your-best conditions.

n.sample_role: Participants in the two mutually exclusive Problem 11 comparison conditions, summed from reported condition counts.
n.exclusions: No further exclusions stated for these problem-specific counts.
n.quote:
Which plan will you choose? [Do your best, N ⫽ 65]           Plan N (24%)
        Which plan will you choose? [Save $250,000, N ⫽ 66] Plan N (47%)

es.quote:
Which plan will you choose? [Do your best, N ⫽ 65]           Plan N (24%)
        Which plan will you choose? [Save $250,000, N ⫽ 66] Plan N (47%)

   The number of people who choose the more risky Plan N doubles when
people have a specific rather than a ‘‘do your best’’ goal (p ⬍ .01 by χ 2 ).

notes: Plan N 24% versus 47% and p < .01 by chi-square are reported; numeric chi-square statistic is not printed. Only assigned fields are completion targets; remaining entries are placeholders or supplemental same-test evidence. No conversions. Document identity verified: Goals as Reference Points, Heath/Larrick/Wu, Cognitive Psychology 38 (1999), article ID cogp.1998.0708. Input names no PDF; PDF layout inspection is unavailable. Analytic N arithmetic: 65 + 66 = 131 from the explicitly labeled Problem 11 groups.
